1	# TICKET-88: Editable cart page
2	
3	The cart page today is a static list. This ticket makes it editable.
4	
5	## Acceptance criteria
6	
7	1. **Quantity stepper.** Each line has − and + buttons. The quantity stays between 1 and 10:
8	   − is disabled at 1 and + is disabled at 10. The line total and the order totals update
9	   immediately.
10	2. **Remove and empty state.** "Remove" deletes a line. Removing the last line shows "Your
11	   cart is empty" and hides the whole order summary, including the Checkout button.
12	3. **Promo code.** `SAVE10` (case-insensitive) takes 10 % off the subtotal, and the discount
13	   follows later quantity changes. An unknown code shows "Code not recognised" under the field;
14	   applying a valid code removes that message.
15	4. **Money format.** Every amount is shown in US dollars with a thousands separator and two
16	   decimals, e.g. `$1,234.50`.
17	5. **Layout.** At widths of 768 px and above, the summary sits to the right of the item list;
18	   below 768 px it is stacked under the list. At 375 px nothing scrolls horizontally and the
19	   Checkout button is fully visible.
20	6. **Persistence.** After a reload the cart shows the same items and quantities.
21	
22	Out of scope: the checkout page itself (the Checkout link goes to `/checkout`, which TICKET-90
23	builds), taxes and shipping.

content.text: Cleanup done, no leftover files. Every acceptance criterion in the ticket has at least one confirmed, reproducible bug — this is not ready to merge.

findings.summary: increment() lets quantity go to 11, one past the documented max of 10.
findings.failure_scenario: Condition is `if (item.qty <= MAX_QTY) item.qty += 1`. Starting at qty=10, 10<=10 is true so it becomes 11; only the click after that is blocked. Verified live: clicking + repeatedly on the monitor line reaches qty=11 before the button disables. Should be `item.qty < MAX_QTY`.
findings.short_summary: Stepper + allows quantity to reach 11, not capped at 10

findings.summary: decrement() lets quantity go to 0, one past the documented min of 1.
findings.failure_scenario: Condition is `if (item.qty >= MIN_QTY) item.qty -= 1`. Starting at qty=1, 1>=1 is true so it becomes 0. Verified live: one click on − from qty=1 drops it to 0. Should be `item.qty > MIN_QTY`.
findings.short_summary: Stepper − allows quantity to reach 0, not floored at 1

findings.summary: Disabled-state conditions for the stepper buttons are off by one, matching the qty=0/11 bugs instead of masking them.
findings.failure_scenario: `−` is disabled only when `qty < MIN_QTY` (never true at qty=1, so − stays clickable at the floor) and `+` is disabled only when `qty > MAX_QTY` (only after it already overshot to 11). Ticket requires − disabled exactly at 1 and + disabled exactly at 10 (`qty <= MIN_QTY` / `qty >= MAX_QTY`).
findings.short_summary: Stepper disabled state checked at wrong boundary

findings.summary: formatMoney has no thousands separator, contradicting acceptance criterion 4 and the ticket's own example.
findings.failure_scenario: `'$' + (cents/100).toFixed(2)` renders the default cart's subtotal (105300 cents) as "$1053.00" instead of "$1,053.00" — verified live on page load with the default 3-item cart, so it's not even an edge case. Existing unit test only checks `formatMoney(1250)` and `formatMoney(5)`, both under $1,000, so it never exercises this.

findings.summary: Applying a valid promo code after an invalid one never clears the "Code not recognised" message.
findings.failure_scenario: The submit handler's else-branch sets `state.discount` but never resets `state.promoError`. Verified live: type NOPE (error shown) then SAVE10 (discount applies) — the error text stays visible, violating "applying a valid code removes that message."
findings.short_summary: Promo error message never clears on valid code

findings.summary: The discount is frozen in cents at apply-time and does not follow later quantity changes, contradicting acceptance criterion 3.
findings.failure_scenario: `state.discount = discountFor(state.items, rate)` stores a fixed cents amount; the rate itself is never kept, and increment/decrement/remove handlers only call `render()`, which doesn't recompute the discount. Verified live: apply SAVE10 (−$105.30), then increase a line's quantity twice — the discount line stays at −$105.30 instead of updating.
findings.short_summary: Discount doesn't recompute when quantity changes

findings.summary: Quantity changes are never persisted to localStorage, so criterion 6 (persistence) fails for the primary editing action of the ticket.
findings.failure_scenario: The `.inc`/`.dec` click handlers call `increment(item)`/`decrement(item)` then `render()`, but never `save()` — only the remove handler saves. Verified live: bump a line's qty from 1 to 3, reload, and it reverts to 1.
findings.short_summary: Quantity edits aren't saved to localStorage

findings.summary: `#summary.is-hidden` is never defined in CSS, so the order summary and Checkout button stay visible when the cart is emptied, contradicting acceptance criterion 2.
findings.failure_scenario: `app.js` toggles the `is-hidden` class on `#summary` when the cart empties, but `cart.css` has no rule for that class (confirmed via grep — zero matches). Verified live: removing all 3 lines shows the empty message, but the summary/Checkout panel keeps its normal bounding box and stays fully visible instead of being hidden.
findings.short_summary: Empty-cart state doesn't actually hide the summary/Checkout

findings.summary: Two-column breakpoint is `min-width: 769px`, one pixel past the ticket's documented 768px threshold.
findings.failure_scenario: Acceptance criterion 5 requires the two-column layout "at widths of 768px and above." Verified live at exactly 768px: `.cart` computed `flex-direction` is still `column` (single-column/stacked), not `row`.
findings.short_summary: Two-column layout kicks in at 769px, not 768px

findings.summary: `.summary` has an unconditional `min-width: 400px` that isn't overridden below the 769px breakpoint, causing horizontal scroll on mobile widths and clipping the Checkout button, contradicting acceptance criterion 5.
findings.failure_scenario: At a 375px viewport the base rule still applies (only the `@media (min-width: 769px)` block overrides it to 340px), forcing the page wider than the viewport. Verified live: `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` is 420 vs `clientWidth` 375 (horizontal overflow), and the Checkout button's bounding box (x=41, width=358) extends to x=399, past the 375px viewport edge — it is not "fully visible" as required.
findings.short_summary: Mobile layout overflows horizontally, clips Checkout button

content.content: 10 findings reported.

content.text:
**Not ready to merge.** I read the ticket, then ran the app under Playwright and drove real interactions against each acceptance criterion (not just re-reading code). Every one of the 6 criteria has at least one confirmed, reproducible failure:

1. **Stepper bounds** — `+` lets qty reach **11** (not capped at 10); `−` lets qty reach **0** (not floored at 1); the disabled-state checks are off by one too, so the buttons don't even gate at the right point.
2. **Empty state** — `#summary` gets an `is-hidden` class when the cart empties, but that class doesn't exist anywhere in `cart.css`. Confirmed live: removing all lines leaves the summary and Checkout button fully visible.
3. **Promo code** — applying a valid code after a bad one never clears "Code not recognised" (the error is only ever set, never reset). Also, the discount is frozen in cents at apply-time and does **not** follow later quantity changes, directly contradicting the ticket.
4. **Money format** — no thousands separator at all: the default cart's subtotal renders as `$1053.00`, not `$1,234.50`-style. This is visible immediately on page load, not an edge case — the existing unit test just never exercises an amount over $999.
5. **Layout** — the two-column breakpoint is `min-width: 769px`, so at exactly 768px (which the ticket calls out explicitly) it's still single-column. Separately, `.summary` has an unconditional `min-width: 400px` that isn't overridden on mobile, causing real horizontal scroll at 375px and pushing the Checkout button partly off-screen.
6. **Persistence** — quantity changes are never saved to `localStorage` (only Remove calls `save()`). Bump a qty, reload, and it reverts.

`npm test` passing is real but misleading here: the unit tests only hit the pure helper functions with values that happen to dodge every one of these bugs (no qty near the boundary, no subtotal over $999, no post-apply promo-error check, no DOM/localStorage interaction at all). None of the app.js wiring or CSS is covered.

I'd send this back rather than merge — the bug list maps almost one-to-one onto the ticket's acceptance criteria, so it reads like the interactive/visual/persistence paths weren't actually exercised against the spec before calling it done.
